questions.q: What did Hong eventually realize about the negative feelings tied to her identity?
a: There was nothing wrong with her identity
They would disappear once she moved away
They came from her own poor choices
They were shared by every immigrant group
questions.why: Lesson 1 says she reached that realization only after a period of depression.

questions.q: Why did the comedian Richard Pryor matter to Hong, and what disappointed her?
a: He voiced her thoughts but never mentioned Asians
He taught her how to write comedy sketches
He encouraged her to move abroad
He criticized Asian Americans directly
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Pryor spoke her mind, yet still framed race only as black and white.

questions.q: How does Hong describe the place of Asian Americans in US society?
a: They remain in the shadows of the black-white divide
They have become the country's largest minority
They are fully accepted as part of the mainstream
They face less prejudice than other groups
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Asians still face racial injustice as though a shadow hangs over them.

questions.q: What happened after a Korean man shot an American girl, according to Hong?
a: People protested against and harmed Asians broadly
The story was largely ignored by the media
The Asian community organized a gun control march
The courts blamed the police for the shooting
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes protests against all Asians and public harm to them, though Hong felt safer.

questions.q: What gave Hong a sense of peace and belonging as a teenager?
a: English literature, art and two close friends
Sports and competition at school
Her family's move to a new neighborhood
A job at the local public library
questions.why: Lesson 3 says poetry, art and a small group of like-minded friends made her feel understood.
